title: Agent Grid client servers
description: The canonical client configuration contract, shared by every client host: web host, terminal CLI, Workspace and Windows Shell. No loader validates against this document — each language holds one hand-written loader, because wire and persistence types stay stdlib-only. What keeps the three honest is x-contract-rules below plus the expected-outcome corpus in fixtures/servers-corpus.json, which every loader asserts against.

x-admission.description: Admission is per entry. A malformed entry costs that entry and the entries it collides with, not the fleet. Only an unreadable entry list stops a host, because that is the one case where no entry can be named. A loader never renames, normalises, suffixes, disables or drops an entry to resolve a violation.

states.usable: Valid and enabled; this entry is connected to.
states.disabled: Valid but not enabled; never connected to, and not an error.
states.configuration_invalid: Broke a rule, or collides with an entry that did. Never probed, never connected to, and always reported with its position, its display name as written, and the rule it violates.

x-contract-rules.statement: The document is JSON; an unparseable file stops the host.
schema_version equals 2 exactly; no version is migrated or rewritten.
servers is present and is an array. An empty array is an empty fleet, not an error.
Every entry carries a display_name that is not blank after trimming.
A display name contains no ASCII control character and does not begin with '-', so it is usable as a command-line argument.
Among enabled entries, display names are unique by exact code-point equality after trimming. Every member of a collision is invalid; no winner is chosen.
display_name and url are strings; enabled and default_execution are booleans.
An unrecognised entry field is rejected; only the deprecated id field is accepted and discarded.
A gateway URL is absolute with scheme http or https.
Credentials, a query or a fragment in a gateway URL are rejected, not stripped.
The canonical URL lower-cases scheme and host, drops a default port, and removes trailing path slashes.
serverId is srv_ plus the lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical URL; it is never read from the file.
Two entries may not resolve to the same canonical URL. Every member of a collision is invalid; no winner is chosen.
At most one entry carries default_execution. When more do, every marked entry is invalid.
A document with no default_execution marker uses its first usable entry, without being rewritten.

id.description: Ignored read-only compatibility field; clients derive the identifier from url.

display_name.description: Addressable server name. Unique among enabled entries by exact code-point equality after trimming; no ASCII control character; must not begin with '-'.

default_execution.description: Marks the enabled server selected by default for new sessions. Older files without this field use the first enabled entry until saved.
